title: Greg Roberts: OU Guard Who Won the 1978 Outland Trophy
question: Which Oklahoma lineman won the Outland Trophy in 1978?
answer: Guard Greg Roberts won the 1978 Outland Trophy, becoming the fourth Sooner to earn the award for the nation's best interior lineman. He was a consensus All-American that year while blocking for Heisman winner Billy Sims.
summary: Greg Roberts won the 1978 Outland Trophy as OU's right guard, the fourth Sooner to win it, opening holes for Billy Sims and the nation's top rushing team.
body: When Oklahoma needed yards in 1978, the play often went right behind Greg Roberts. The guard from Nacogdoches, Texas, was so central to Barry Switzer's offense that OU's history notes most of the Sooners' plays that fall ran over his right guard spot. That season he won the Outland Trophy, becoming the fourth Sooner to take the award.

Roberts played at Oklahoma from 1975 through 1978. He earned All-America recognition as a junior in 1977 and then became a consensus All-American as a senior. He was also named UPI Lineman of the Year in 1978 and was a two-time first-team All-Big Eight selection.

The results spoke for themselves. With Roberts leading the way, OU led the nation in scoring and rushing in 1978 and finished second in total offense. His speed and strength helped open running lanes for Billy Sims, who won the Heisman Trophy that fall, so the Sooners claimed both the Heisman and the Outland in the same year.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected Roberts in the second round of the 1979 NFL Draft, 33rd overall. He made the PFWA All-Rookie Team, played four seasons in Tampa from 1979 to 1982, and later suited up for the USFL's Memphis Showboats in 1984.
Roberts' 1978 Outland would be the last one for Oklahoma for 26 years, until offensive tackle Jammal Brown brought the trophy back to Norman in 2004.
